concerns.text: The plan states "No min‑max scaling (FR‑010 revised)" which directly contradicts the functional requirement FR‑010 in the spec that mandates min‑max scaling of the FQY target computed on the training set. This inconsistency undermines construct validity of the target variable and may affect loss stability.

The power analysis assumes an effect size yielding R² ≥ 0.7 (Cohen’s f² ≈ 2.33) without providing empirical justification or citation. Such a large effect size is optimistic for fluorescence quantum yield prediction and may lead to under‑powered experiments if the true effect is smaller.

Attribution validation relies on a curated fluorophore‑motif list (Supplementary Table S1) and claims independence from training/test splits, but the plan only mentions a “cross‑check” without describing how the motif list is constructed or verified to be disjoint. This raises risk of circular validation and threatens the validity of SC‑005.

The plan requires ≥ 200 matched molecules after join and a minimum test set of 70 molecules (≈ 35 % of data) while also enforcing a scaffold‑based 80/10/10 split with zero scaffold overlap. For many chemical datasets, achieving both a large test set and strict scaffold disjointness may be infeasible, potentially causing the pipeline to abort or produce a biased split.
